numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Summing a large float64 array through einsum loses precision because the nditer flags no longer include NPY_ITER_GROWINNER, so the reduction is not chunked. The sum drifts from the true value for large sums with nonzero mean.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Large float64 einsum sums should keep chunked (GROWINNER-style) accumulation so the result is as precise as before the nditer refactor; the test checks that np.einsum('i->', np.full(num, value)) / num stays precise for num=100000000 and value=1.00000000002. The exact tolerance is not given in the passages.
trigger_conditions: float64 reduction in einsum over a very large 1-D array (example uses 100000000 elements)
array values with nonzero mean, so accumulated rounding error grows with length
einsum path using the buffered nditer iteration in PyArray_EinsteinSum without NPY_ITER_GROWINNER

input_output_examples.buggy_output: lower-precision result than before the nditer refactor (exact value not given in passages)

numerical_characteristics.precision: Passages show the test asserts agreement to decimal=15 for float64 sums (np.finfo(np.float64).eps*8196 offset); the GROWINNER removal note says chunking gives partially stable summation for float64; sklearn noticed lower precision; no explicit single tolerance beyond decimal=15 is stated as the separation threshold.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Large sums: num = 1_000_000 elements (broadcast array) and num = 100000000 elements (np.full) where the mean is nonzero; chunking improves precision for large sums with nonzero mean.
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: assert_almost_equal with decimal=15 for the 1,000,000-element case; the passages do not state a separate threshold separating correct and incorrect answers.
category_specific_evidence: Commit/PR: nditer refactor enabled GROWINNER for reductions, dropping chunking, which reduced precision of large einsum sums (sklearn reported it, issue #30509).
Fix removes NPY_ITER_GROWINNER from iter_flags in einsum.c.src PyArray_EinsteinSum, with a comment that this gives partially stable summation for float64 and pairwise summation would be better.
Test test_einsum adds a 1_000_000-element broadcast sum checked with assert_almost_equal decimal=15, and a 100000000-element np.full(value=1.00000000002) sum divided by num.
Comment in test: at GROWINNER 11 decimals succeed (larger will be less); a note says it is unclear precision should be guaranteed to this extent.
Performance trade-off: roughly 1% slowdown for the simplest einsum('i,i->i', x, x) case.
reproduction_risks: Whether GROWINNER is active depends on the nditer buffering/chunk size, which the passages do not specify numerically.
The 100000000-element case is very large and may be impractical; the passages give no alternative size.
Test comment about 11 decimals versus decimal=15 is internally inconsistent in the passages, so the exact threshold is uncertain.
Precision guarantee is explicitly described as unclear, so exact expected values may be unstable across platforms.
